description: Web Agent workbench: agent list/detail pages, profile management, generic AgentSession composer/detail/transcript, follow-up, and Ask Agent quick entries — web-only, consuming the completed #128/#129/#130 backend APIs.

tasks.title: Agent data layer: CRUD query hooks and generic AgentSession client/hooks
tasks.description: Add the missing TanStack Query layer for Agent profile CRUD (useAgents, useAgent, useCreateAgent, useUpdateAgent, useArchiveAgent) following existing issue/epic query conventions, wrapping the low-level client fns already present in entities/agent/api/client.ts. Add a new generic-AgentSession client module (entities/agent/api/agent-sessions.ts) with pure client fns and matching query/mutation hooks consuming the #129 launch/followup/cancel and #130 generic summary/transcript endpoints. All hooks use projectApiPath + the shared request envelope and are enabled only when projectId is present. This is the foundational data layer every subsequent UI task consumes.
acceptanceCriteria: useAgents() and useAgent(agentRef) return typed AgentInfo, query-keyed ['agents', projectId] and ['agents', projectId, agentRef] respectively, enabled only when projectId is present
useCreateAgent, useUpdateAgent, useArchiveAgent mutations call the existing client fns and invalidate ['agents'] (and ['agent-status'] for launch-affecting changes) on success

getGenericSessionSummary(sessionId), getGenericSessionTranscript(sessionId), launchAgentSession(agentRef, { prompt, context }), postGenericFollowup(sessionId, text), cancelGenericSession(sessionId) client fns exist over projectApiPath + request envelope matching the #129/#130 endpoint contracts
useGenericSessionSummary and useGenericSessionTranscript hooks are query-keyed ['agent-session', projectId, sessionId] (+ '/transcript'), enabled only when projectId is present

useLaunchAgentSession, useGenericFollowup, useCancelGenericSession mutations invalidate ['agent-status'], ['agent-activity'], the owning ['agents', projectId, agentRef, 'sessions'] list, and the relevant ['agent-session', …] query on success
All client fns and hooks are covered by unit tests against faked responses (no real API calls per test policy)
Barrel re-exports updated in entities/agent/index.ts
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes
tasks.notes: Design D4 (CRUD hooks) + D5 (generic session client). The low-level CRUD client fns (listAgents/getAgent/createAgent/updateAgent/archiveAgent) and model helpers (readAgentModelAndVariant/writeAgentModelAndVariant) already exist in client.ts — this task adds the Query/mutation layer on top. No #129/#130 client wrapper exists yet.

tasks.title: Generalize SessionPage for generic AgentSession via SessionDataSource seam
tasks.description: Extract a SessionDataSource interface and a shared SessionDetailShell from the existing SessionPage (~1000 lines, hard-coupled to issueNumber). Provide two implementations: IssueSessionDataSource (wrapping the current issue-scoped client fns and recovery actions — regression-free) and GenericAgentSessionDataSource (consuming T-001's generic hooks). Add a buildGenericSessionMetadata adapter mapping GenericAgentSessionSummaryDto to the internal SessionMetadata (workflow-only fields absent: stage null, runtimeSessionLineage empty, issueId empty). Generalize SessionFollowupComposer to accept an injected onSend callback instead of the hardwired useFollowupMutation. For generic sessions, omit Compact/Reset recovery actions (no endpoint) while keeping ContextHealthBar and CompactionLineageLink when data is present. Register the agent-sessions/:sessionId route through GenericAgentSessionDataSource. The transcript rendering subtree (widgets/session-transcript/*) is reused unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Issue-scoped session routes (issues/:number/session/:sessionId, issues/:number/workflow/sessions/:sessionName) render through IssueSessionDataSource with no behavior change — existing session-page tests pass unchanged (regression gate)
agent-sessions/:sessionId route renders a generic session via GenericAgentSessionDataSource, consuming T-001's useGenericSessionSummary and useGenericSessionTranscript hooks
Generic session detail displays transcript, status, usage, failure category (when failed), and context references without requiring an owning issue or workflow stage

Generic session header links back to the owning Agent profile (/agents/{agentId}), or to the referenced issue when an issue context ref exists; omits workflow-stage badge and owning-issue link rather than fabricating them
SessionFollowupComposer accepts an injected onSend(text) callback; issue-scoped call site passes the issue-scoped mutation, generic detail page passes useGenericFollowup
Follow-up composer is enabled for non-terminal (running/recoverable) sessions and disabled/hidden for terminal (completed/failed) sessions, driven by shared statusKind
Recovery region: ContextHealthBar and CompactionLineageLink render for generic sessions when data present; Compact/Reset actions omitted (no endpoint)
Header-above-transcript, sticky recovery bar, compaction summary atop transcript, and responsive behaviors apply uniformly to both issue-scoped and generic sources
Tests cover: generic session detail rendering, header back-link logic (agent vs issue ref), follow-up enable/disable, recovery region omission, and IssueSessionDataSource regression
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes
tasks.output: packages/web/src/pages/session/ (SessionDetailShell, SessionDataSource interface + impls), packages/web/src/widgets/coder-session/ui/SessionFollowupComposer.tsx (generalized), agent-sessions/:sessionId route in app/App.tsx, buildGenericSessionMetadata adapter, tests
tasks.notes: Design D2 (SessionDataSource seam) + D3 (metadata adapter) + D7 (followup generalization) + D8 (recovery bar). The transcript subtree (widgets/session-transcript/* — SessionTranscriptLayout, TurnList, PromptBlock, AssistantParts, tool-views, ContextHealthBar, CompactionLineageLink) operates purely on SessionTurn/DisplayTurn with no issue dependency and is reused unchanged. D2 explicitly rejects in-place conditionals (9 coupling points) in favor of the shell+datasource approach.

tasks.title: Agent list & detail pages with profile management UI
tasks.description: Add AgentListPage (browse all profiles — active and archived, distinguishable — with runtime/config summary, most recent session, and availability status; empty state when no profiles exist), AgentDetailPage (profile summary of instructions/agentConfig/skills + session history grouped client-side into recent/running/failed/ended sections using a single useAgentSessions query; edit/archive entry points; archived profiles clearly marked with launch disabled), and a profile editor widget (create/edit/archive via T-001 CRUD hooks; instructions textarea, ModelSelect for model+variant reusing the IssueModelSelector pattern, skills metadata; required-field validation and inline API error surfacing). Register routes (agents, agents/:agentId), add the Agents sidebar nav entry and mobile nav tab, and extend usePageTitle in Header.tsx. Context refs in session history items and the new-session entry point use the D1 URL convention (agent-sessions/:sessionId, agent-sessions/new?agent=) — these links become fully functional once T-002 and T-004 land.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Agents' entry present in primary sidebar navigation and mobile bottom nav; selecting it navigates to the Agent list page scoped to the current project
Agent list enumerates every profile (active and archived, visually distinguishable); each row displays name, agent type, model, variant, most recent session, and availability status
List renders an empty state explaining no agents are defined and offering a create entry when the project has no profiles
Agent detail page renders profile instructions, agent config (model + variant), and skills metadata
Detail page renders sessions grouped into recent, running, failed, and ended lifecycle sections from a single useAgentSessions({ agentRef }) query (client-side grouping, no N filtered round-trips)
Detail page offers a new-session entry for active profiles that navigates to the composer pre-selected to that profile; archived profiles are clearly marked and the launch entry is disabled
Profile editor creates a profile via CRUD API and navigates to the new profile's detail page on success
Profile editor persists edits (instructions, agentConfig via ModelSelect, skills) via CRUD API and reflects updated values on the detail page
Profile editor archives a profile via CRUD API; archived profile remains listed but distinguished and not launchable
Editor blocks submission with missing required fields and surfaces inline validation errors on offending fields
Tests cover: list rendering + empty state, detail summary + session grouping, editor create/edit/archive/validation flows, archived launch disabling

tasks.title: New-session composer with context refs and launch
tasks.description: Add AgentSessionComposerPage at route agent-sessions/new (declared before agent-sessions/:sessionId so the literal wins). The page reads query params (?agent=<ref>, ?issue=<n>, ?epic=<ref>, ?repo=, ?ws=) to pre-select the agent and pre-fill context references. Prompt textarea reuses AttachmentComposer; context refs render as removable chips. Required-field validation enforces prompt-required and disables launch for archived agents. Launch calls useLaunchAgentSession; on 201 { sessionId } it navigates to agent-sessions/:sessionId (T-002's route). Context is passed ONLY as the launch body's context envelope — never creating scope/mount/supervisor lifecycle. Surface dedicated error states for 'no available runner' and 'external agent unavailable'.
acceptanceCriteria: agent-sessions/new route is declared before agent-sessions/:sessionId in App.tsx so the literal segment wins
Composer reads ?agent=, ?issue=, ?epic=, ?repo=, ?ws= query params (with encodeURIComponent on emitted params) to pre-select agent and pre-fill context refs
Agent selector lists profiles via useAgents() from T-001; archived agents are selectable but disable launch
Prompt is required — launch is blocked without a prompt and the composer indicates a prompt is required
Context references (issue, epic, repository, workspace path) render as removable chips and are passed as session metadata in the launch body context envelope only
Launch calls the #129 endpoint via useLaunchAgentSession with the selected profile, prompt, and context refs; on success navigates to agent-sessions/:sessionId
Context refs do NOT cause creation of workflow scope, mount configuration, or supervisor lifecycle
'No available runner' error state surfaces a clear message for the selected agent type and prevents launch
'External agent unavailable' error state surfaces a clear message and prevents launching until recovery
Tests cover: query-param parsing and pre-fill, agent selection, prompt validation, launch call + navigation, context-ref chip add/remove, archived-agent launch disabling, and both error states

tasks.notes: Design D6. AttachmentComposer (shared/ui/attachment-composer/) is the prompt textarea base. v1 accepts explicit refs (from Ask Agent entries and manual ?issue=) — a dedicated ContextRefPicker autocomplete is deferred (Open Question). Launch status may return inactive until a runner binds; the composer navigates to the detail page immediately and the summary query advances running → terminal; the error states cover the stuck-inactive case.

tasks.title: Ask Agent quick entries on issue, epic, and project pages
tasks.description: Add a compact 'Ask Agent' entry to IssueDetailPage (action cluster / right-rail Actions CardSection), EpicDetailPage (action cluster), and DashboardPage (project surface hero/zone button). Each entry navigates to /agent-sessions/new with the current entity pre-filled as a context reference query param (?issue=<number>, ?epic=<id>, or no ref for project — project is the implicit URL scope). Entries only pre-fill context metadata and introduce no supervisor, mount, or workflow configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: IssueDetailPage exposes an 'Ask Agent' entry that navigates to the composer with ?issue=<number> pre-filled
EpicDetailPage exposes an 'Ask Agent' entry that navigates to the composer with ?epic=<id> pre-filled
DashboardPage exposes an 'Ask Agent' entry that navigates to the composer (project is implicit scope, no explicit ref)
Each entry only pre-fills context metadata — no supervisor, mount, or workflow configuration is created
Emitted query params are encodeURIComponent'd, matching the existing projectPath convention
Tests cover navigation URL construction and context pre-fill for each of the three entry points
